messages:
maria: Quick q — how should we surface the 'changeproof' delivery guarantees in Console + Export API? Thinking signed proof bundles vs streaming NDJSON + webhook acks. cc @ajay @kevin
ajay: my vote is: REST download (signed bundle) for compliance downloads, streaming/webhook for live consumers. different SLA surfaces in console.
kevin: Agree. Also need to account for routing policies: if a request falls back to a cheaper model/region, do we still attach the same proof metadata?
sasha: we should include provenance headers regardless of fallback. minimal shape: {actor, timestamp, model_id, route_origin, proof_sig?} — and make proof_sig optional for streaming.
maria: yeah — console should show provenance as a compact row, with a "Download signed proof" CTA that triggers bundle creation/retention policy.
toni: UX question — do we expose bundle size estimates and expected prep time? large backfills could take mins.
ajay: yes. show ETA and token count. default: async bundle with presigned link. for live webhook delivery include per-tenant max parallel deliveries (quota).
kevin: technical: export delivery matrix needs these axes: delivery_mode={signed-bundle, ndjson-stream, webhook}, routing_tier={hosted,dedicated,private}, fallbacks_allowed={true,false}, retry_policy={immediate, exponential, dead-letter}. then map SLA and cost.
sasha: +1. For NDJSON streaming we should include sequence numbers and last-ack-id so replay is possible. also consider prefix-caching interaction (if cached prefix, proofs still valid?).
audit-bot: Export job queued: id=exp-20250304-42, mode=webhook, tenant=acme-corp
toni: policy question — signed proof retention: default 90 days, enterprise can increase. need consent checkbox and notice in console. legal asked for 12 months on some contracts.
maria: We'll add a console flag per tenant "Require signed proofs for downloads" and show an indicator on routing policy pages if a route will produce signed proofs or not.
ajay: API shape suggestion for webhook ack: POST /export/ack {job_id, sequence_id, status, received_at, signer_hint?} If ack is missing after backoff, move to dead-letter and surface in console alerting.
sasha: Also add a lightweight query endpoint: GET /export/status?job_id=... returns last_sequence, delivered, retries, proof_status. Useful for SRE dashboards.
kevin: Regarding quotas: delivery_quota = max_concurrent_webhook + daily_transfer_limit + burst_tokens. console should show quota usage and estimated time to clear queue.
joni: (ops) can we have an emergency bypass to force signed-bundle generation for legal requests?
maria: yes, add "Generate legal bundle" action in tenant admin with audit guard and justification prompt. logs must capture who clicked and reason.
audit-bot: Export job exp-20250304-42 status=delivering seq=12/120 retries=1
toni: small but important — UI copy for "proof" confused some customers. use "signed audit bundle" in UX copy and tooltip: "cryptographically signed delivery bundle for compliance".
ajay: implementation note: signed bundles are expensive. we should offload signing to a signing-service with HSM and enqueue jobs — maintain per-tenant signing quotas to control cost.
sasha: can we offer an option: ephemeral signed token (short-lived) vs fully-signed bundle for download? some customers only need proof that this payload was emitted, not the whole bundle.
maria: good idea. add to matrix as delivery_variant={full_bundle, proof_token}. show in console and API param.
kevin: last: rollout plan — feature flag gating: start with hosted customers, then dedicated, then private. add telemetry events: export.requested, export.signed_bundle.created, export.webhook.delivered, export.dead_lettered. tie these to billing counters.
maria: I'll draft an RFC with the matrix + API shapes and mockups. action items: @ajay sketch API, @sasha sketch status endpoints + seq model, @kevin write routing tier implications, @toni draft UX copy and retention options.
ajay: on it.
kevin: will do.
sasha: will have a draft by EOD.
toni: I'll pull legal requirements and start draft copy.
